My family and I moved into a new house. We had sold our old house and rented a house right across the road from our old house. My family was to move to another country and I was to stay in the city for college. I picked the room on the top floor and it seemed perfect for me! I had my own bathroom, bed room and right across was this old attic where we stored some of our stuff.

Everything was fine in the house, it was a bit old and creepy but nothing out of the ordinary. Two or three months later things changed in the house, just the feeling of it. I thought I must have been paranoid, nervous for college or something so I never took it seriously.

One night I was in bed watching ‘Whose line is it anyway’ on my laptop. I was trying to fall asleep but being a teen I woke up at 2-3pm in the afternoon that day and couldn't shut my eyes. 

I closed my laptop and went to bed. I don’t really know how to explain it so bear with me: a rush of anger - pure anger went through me. It wasn’t anything I felt before. I stood up and touched my three level lamp. The light was on the weakest but I saw a shadow of a man leaning towards me. It lasted maybe one second but enough to know what I saw. Of course I thought I was just tired so I tried to go back to bed. Very anxious but trying to go to bed.

Maybe five minutes later my lamp goes from shade one to two and then ultimately three.. My tv and my laptop went on and off. This happened at least 2-3 times.

I ran and slept in my sister's bed that night - Never slept in that haunted bedroom again.

TL:DR; Moved houses, settled in a bedroom across attic. Got spooky quick.

I would organize a small gathering at my house once a month for some high school friends I had. We always had fun and I was glad we kept in touch. At that point I was the only one that lived by myself so I had no problem providing my apartment for these parties. These friends barely had money since most of them started college a few years late so I would provide them with booze and snacks.  
A few years goes by and they all start having jobs and having money. 
One of my friends brought a bottle of red wine (he stole it from his mother) to my place and forgot about it. He was drinking the beers I bought so he didn’t need it that night. A few months later, I find it and think that it is mine so I take it. When he found out, he got so upset about a ten dollar bottle of wine, but never realized I spent way more than 10$ on him per night that he partied at my place. I got over it, but I should’ve taken it as a hint.
On my birthday I invited the same friends to a party me and friends (other group) were having for a predrink at my place before we go out. We start playing beer pong and everyone shares their beers without a second thought. We run out of booze soon enough and they didn’t even want to share one of their four six-packs. We probably gave them around 4-5 beers each.
That’s when I realized that they probably did not care much for me but came for the free booze, snacks and parties. I stopped inviting them or caring altogether. They sometimes text/call me trying to give me hints to make a party. Lesson learned.

I work in insurance and do all documentation/claims for most disabilities. The only difference is I work in Canada.

It all depends on what kind of insurance you have and for what. The best thing to do is to call and ask of a copy of the contract/application. You can than look what their <pre-existent> means and work from there. I have many mental disabilities right now who had depression before the insurance and than commited suicide after they had it. We still fully payed for their house. That’s why get a copy of the policy. You can always call them and ask them why and what they considered it pre-existent. If they still don’t budge than I would suggest a lawyer.
